source.section: Schedule M line 47 Senior Citizen Deduction columns (a)-(d) (PDF p.6; instructions PDF p.29; example PDF p.30; PDF p.23 'Taxpayers over age 65 or disabled'; Tax Division page: 'You receive the higher of the $8,000 modification or the sum of various itemized decreasing modifications'); Schedule M line 33(a)-(b) Other Retirement Modification, 'Combined amounts of 33a and 33b must not exceed $2,000' (PDF p.5; instructions PDF p.28; PDF p.22); IT-140 lines 1-8 (PDF p.3; instructions PDF p.26: exemptions 2,000 each, line 7 floored at zero); Rate Schedules I and II (PDF p.37); Tax Table (PDF p.38 on)

worked: Single, age 70, a West Virginia PERS pension 20,000 and an IRA distribution. The form: line 33 2,000 is in column (d), so line 47 is 6,000 and the two come to 8,000. The projection keeps line 33 outside the line 47 group (accepted approximation, understates tax), so it takes 2,000 + 8,000 = 10,000; expected follows the projection. filer born 1955-05-05, age 70 at December 31, 2025. Federal AGI (given) = West Virginia PERS/Teachers' pension 20,000.00 + IRA distribution 10,000.00 = 30,000.00. Federal taxable income (given, not tested) = 30,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 aged 65 or older = 12,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IT-140 line 1 federal AGI 30,000.00. Schedule M additions lines 51-58 none; IT-140 line 2 0.00. Schedule M Column A: line 33(a) WV Teachers'/PERS 2,000.00, line 33(b) federal retirement 0.00; line 33 = lesser of their sum 2,000.00 and 2,000.00 = 2,000.00; line 47 (age 70): column (c) income not on lines 35-46 = 30,000.00, limited to 8,000.00: 8,000.00; column (d) lines 29-34 = 2,000.00; line 47 = 8,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 6,000.00; line 49 = 8,000.00. Line 50 total subtractions = 8,000.00. Projection (per person): The filer: Social Security subtraction 0.00; age 65 deduction = lesser of (8,000.00 - military retirement 0.00) and own income 30,000.00 = 8,000.00; best_of_group wv_line_47 keeps the larger, 8,000.00 (wv_senior_citizen_deduction). Projection subtractions total 10,000.00, where line 50 is 8,000.00 (accepted approximation: line 33 stays outside the line 47 group). By the form instead: line 3 8,000.00, line 4 22,000.00, line 7 20,000.00, tax 518.00; the projection's tax is lower by 59.20. IT-140 line 3 subtractions 10,000.00; line 4 West Virginia AGI = 30,000.00 + 0.00 - 10,000.00 = 20,000.00. Line 5 Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion: federal AGI over 10,000, none. Line 6 exemptions 1 x 2,000.00 = 2,000.00. Line 7 taxable income = 20,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 18,000.00. Line 8 tax by Rate Schedule I (PDF p.37) bands: 2.22% x 10,000.00 = 222 + 2.96% x 8,000.00 = 236.8; total 458.8 = 458.80. The Tax Table row 18,000 to under 18,100 (PDF p.38 on) gives 460; expected keeps the schedule formula on the exact income. No Family Tax Credit (Modified Federal AGI above the table limits); credits 0.00; state income tax 458.80.
accepted_approximations: Line 47 takes that person's lines 29 through 34 off the 8,000, so together they come to the higher of the two. The format cannot say that: cap_reduced_by takes off benefits received, and line 34 is only the taxable benefits at 65% or 100%. So the Social Security subtraction and the age 65 deduction share a best_of_group, each person's larger one counting, with the 8,000 reduced by military retirement. That is exact for Social Security and military retirement. Line 33 stays outside the group because a person under 65 keeps it alongside Social Security, and a whole public pension can't be taken off the 8,000 when only 2,000 of it is on line 33.

Tax below 100,000 of taxable income is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses a Tax Table row's midpoint rounded to the whole dollar. Other tax is also rounded to the whole dollar in the booklet.
